From 3dd4d40b420846dd35869ccc8f8627feef2cff32 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Date: Wed, 23 Oct 2019 17:00:45 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] xfs: Sanity check flags of Q_XQUOTARM call

Flags passed to Q_XQUOTARM were not sanity checked for invalid values.
Fix that.

Fixes: 9da93f9b7cdf ("xfs: fix Q_XQUOTARM ioctl")
Reported-by: Yang Xu <xuyang2018.jy@cn.fujitsu.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Reviewed-by: Eric Sandeen <sandeen@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>

diff --git a/fs/xfs/xfs_quotaops.c b/fs/xfs/xfs_quotaops.c
index cd6c7210a373..c7de17deeae6 100644
--- a/fs/xfs/xfs_quotaops.c
+++ b/fs/xfs/xfs_quotaops.c
@@ -201,6 +201,9 @@ xfs_fs_rm_xquota(
 	if (XFS_IS_QUOTA_ON(mp))
 		return -EINVAL;
 
+	if (uflags & ~(FS_USER_QUOTA | FS_GROUP_QUOTA | FS_PROJ_QUOTA))
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	if (uflags & FS_USER_QUOTA)
 		flags |= XFS_DQ_USER;
 	if (uflags & FS_GROUP_QUOTA)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `fs/xfs/xfs_quotaops.c`**
- Added a sanity check for the `uflags` variable in the `xfs_fs_rm_xquota` function.
- The new check ensures that `uflags` does not contain any invalid flags by using a bitwise AND operation with the negation of valid flags (`FS_USER_QUOTA`, `FS_GROUP_QUOTA`, `FS_PROJ_QUOTA`). If invalid flags are detected, the function returns `-EINVAL`.

### Relationships
The modification addresses a bug related to the `Q_XQUOTARM` ioctl call by ensuring that the flags passed to it are valid. This change is a direct response to a previously reported issue (identified by the commit hash `9da93f9b7cdf`), which lacked proper validation of the flags. The patch improves the robustness of the code by preventing invalid flag values from being processed, thereby enhancing the overall stability of the quota management functionality in the XFS filesystem.

xfs: Sanity check flags of Q_XQUOTARM call

Fixes: 9da93f9b7cdf ("xfs: fix Q_XQUOTARM ioctl")
Reported-by: Yang Xu <xuyang2018.jy@cn.fujitsu.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Reviewed-by: Eric Sandeen <sandeen@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the lack of sanity checks on the flags passed to the `Q_XQUOTARM` ioctl call, allowing invalid flag values to be processed, which could lead to unexpected behavior or errors in the quota management functionality.

Here is the patch:
 
 STATIC int
 xfs_fs_rm_xquota(
 	struct super_block	*sb,
 	unsigned int		uflags)
 {
 	struct xfs_mount	*mp = XFS_M(sb);
 	unsigned int		flags = 0;
 
 	if (sb_rdonly(sb))
 		return -EROFS;
 
 	if (XFS_IS_QUOTA_ON(mp))
 		return -EINVAL;
 
+	if (uflags & ~(FS_USER_QUOTA | FS_GROUP_QUOTA | FS_PROJ_QUOTA))
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	if (uflags & FS_USER_QUOTA)
 		flags |= XFS_DQ_USER;
 	if (uflags & FS_GROUP_QUOTA)
 		flags |= XFS_DQ_GROUP;
 	if (uflags & FS_PROJ_QUOTA)
 		flags |= XFS_DQ_PROJ;
 
 	return xfs_qm_scall_trunc_qfiles(mp, flags);
 }

```c

```
Reason:
The lack of sanity checks on the `uflags` variable allows invalid flag values to be processed. This means that if `uflags` contains any bits set that are not defined by the valid flags (`FS_USER_QUOTA`, `FS_GROUP_QUOTA`, `FS_PROJ_QUOTA`), it could lead to unexpected behavior or errors in the quota management functionality.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+	if (uflags & ~(FS_USER_QUOTA | FS_GROUP_QUOTA | FS_PROJ_QUOTA))
+		return -EINVAL;
```
Reason:
This added check ensures that any invalid flag values in `uflags` are caught before further processing. If `uflags` contains bits that are not part of the defined flags, the function will return an error code `-EINVAL`, preventing the function from executing with invalid parameters and thus maintaining the integrity of the quota management system.
